raidSayLines.line: A man, maybe 50s, with calloused knuckles: "Nothing grows here but dirt and tents. Past the treeline — that's where the green is. That's where the food is."
📓 Journal: Food won't come to Haven. Walk past the treeline — learn what grows out there, bring it back, and get it named at camp.

🛡️ Dawn at Haven. By the fire hangs an old bark cuirass, split at the seam — somebody's grandfather wore this into the treeline and came back. The shape of it is clear: bark plates laced overlapping like shingles, vine cord. Your hands don't know it yet. Your eyes do.
Night. The treeline is just a sound now. The fire is the whole argument against it.
The raccoon with too many fingers stops at the treeline — pacing, unwilling. The walls end the argument. It's still out there.

🦎 "Those were CALIBRATION fauna! First drafts! The audience has NOTES! So we made BETTER ones!" (Something new is crying in the treeline.)

You don't know what that was. A dog-shaped silence at the treeline. Someone at the haven should hear about this.
Three shapes at the treeline — dog-shaped silences, circling. (A real pack is out there now: 3 of them. No names yet — nobody's lived to argue about one.)
Night. The treeline is just a sound now. The fire is the whole argument against it.

🌒 Dusk. They come out of the treeline in a knot — 3 of them, thin and road-worn — and stop at the edge of your firelight like they're not sure they're allowed closer. The oldest steps forward. "Lucia Weiss. From Thornfield." A pause. "We're asking for a fire."
Night. The treeline is just a sound now. The fire is the whole argument against it.

💬 Gadiel pulls you aside. "I need to tell you something. Last night I... dreamed? No. I was AWAKE. And something spoke to me. Not the System — something else. It said: 'Tell the human to watch the northern treeline.' Then it was gone."
Night. The treeline is just a sound now. The fire is the whole argument against it.
Raj came back from the treeline white-faced. Saw it too. Whatever it is, it's still out there.
